explanation: Compound assignment operators in C combine an arithmetic or bitwise operation with an assignment.  They provide a shorter, more concise way to update a variable's value by performing an operation on its current value. This improves code readability and can sometimes lead to slightly more efficient code because the left-hand operand is only evaluated once.

extraction_metadata.source: The C Programming Language - Kernighan & Ritchie

book: The C Programming Language - Kernighan & Ritchie
code_example:
int count = 20;
float rate = 1.5f;
unsigned int flags = 0xF0; // 1111 0000

// Arithmetic Compound Assignment
count += 5;   // count = 25 (count = count + 5)
rate *= 2.0f; // rate = 3.0f (rate = rate * 2.0f)
count /= 8;   // count = 3
count %= 2;   // count = 1

// Bitwise Compound Assignment
flags &= 0x0F; // flags = 0x00 (0xF0 & 0x0F)
flags |= 0xAA; // flags = 0xAA
flags ^= 0xAA; // flags = 0x00 (Toggle off all set bits)
flags <<= 3;   // Shift left by 3
flags >>= 1;   // Shift right by 1
keywords: compound assignment, shorthand operators, augmented assignment, += operator
